learnings.question: In Islamic theology, human purpose on Earth is traditionally described through three primary roles. Which of the following is one of those three roles?
options: Serving as khalifah (steward) of the Earth
learnings.learning: Life's purpose in Islam revolves around three primary roles: worshiping Allah, serving as khalifah (steward) of the Earth, and preparing for the Hereafter through accountability.

learnings.question: In Islamic spirituality, what term describes the mindfulness and awareness of God's presence that builds self-restraint and purifies one's intentions?
learnings.learning: Worship fosters taqwa, an awareness of Allah's presence that builds self-restraint and purifies intentions, guiding a person away from wrongdoing.

learnings.question: Which piece of advice on maintaining unity within a community is attributed to the Prophet Muhammad?
options: Do not hate each other, do not envy each other, and do not turn your backs on each other
Compete with each other in good deeds
Always speak the truth even if it hurts
learnings.learning: The Prophet Muhammad advised against divisive behavior within the community, saying: 'Do not hate each other, do not envy each other, and do not turn your backs on each other.' (Sahih Bukhari 6065)

learnings.question: Linguists have noted a vast difference in vocabulary size between Arabic and English. Approximately what is the ratio of distinct Arabic words to English words listed in the Oxford English Dictionary?
learnings.learning: There are roughly 12 million distinct Arabic words compared to about 170,000 English words in the Oxford English Dictionary, an approximate 71:1 ratio.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: When applying the Pareto Principle (the 80/20 rule) to word frequency in the Quran, what percentage of the text did the 20 most frequently repeated words actually account for, according to one data analysis?
learnings.learning: A data analysis of word frequency in the Quran found that, contrary to the Pareto Principle's 80/20 expectation, the top 20 most repeated words only accumulate to about 20.83% of the text.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what is the key difference between the concepts of 'Qada'' and 'Qadr'?
options: Qada' refers to prayer, while Qadr refers to fasting
Qada' is the actual unfolding of events in life, while Qadr is Allah's complete, eternal plan already written
Qada' is Allah's eternal plan, while Qadr is how events actually unfold
Qada' and Qadr are two different names for the exact same concept with no distinction
learnings.learning: Qada' refers to the actual occurrence of events in life, while Qadr is everything Allah has already planned and written, including all events big or small.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: In the Islamic concept of divine decree, what is said to be capable of changing a person's 'Qada'' (the actual unfolding of their life circumstances)?
options: Nothing — Qada' can never be changed once it begins
Only the intervention of a religious scholar
Sincere Dua (supplication) and one's own actions
Public recognition of one's good deeds
learnings.learning: Qada' can be influenced or altered through sincere Dua (supplication) and one's own actions, though this change was always known to Allah as part of His Qadr.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: Which economist and cognitive scientist, writing in 1971, observed that 'what information consumes is rather obvious: it consumes the attention of its recipients'?
learnings.learning: Herbert Simon wrote in 1971 that in an information-rich world, the wealth of information creates a scarcity of attention, since information consumes the attention of its recipients.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: As a practical response to information overload, what kind of automated system did one software engineer build to filter his daily YouTube video feed?
options: A browser extension that blocks all video thumbnails
A physical timer that locks the phone after 20 minutes
An AI script that asks whether the content would actually benefit him before including it
A paid subscription service that removes ads
learnings.learning: A daily script pulls the latest videos from hand-picked channels and uses AI to ask whether the content would genuinely benefit the viewer, filtering out anything that wouldn't.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: In the Scrum agile framework, what is the purpose of a 'Burndown Chart'?
options: To record attendance at daily stand-up meetings
To list all possible features for the final product
To rank team members by productivity
To visualize the Sprint's progress and show how much work remains
learnings.learning: The Burndown Chart is a Scrum artifact that visualizes the progress of a Sprint, showing remaining work and helping the team track whether they're on schedule.

learnings.question: Which of the following roles is explicitly NOT one of the three key roles defined in the Scrum framework?
learnings.learning: Scrum defines exactly three key roles — Product Owner, Scrum Master, and Developers — with no 'Project Manager' role among them.

learnings.question: Which 19th-century psychologist demonstrated that people forget about 80% of what they learn within 24 hours unless they actively recall it?
learnings.learning: Hermann Ebbinghaus proved back in the 1880s that people forget roughly 80% of what they learn within 24 hours unless they actively force themselves to recall it, which is why spaced repetition works.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: What term describes the psychological phenomenon where writing information down or storing it digitally causes the brain to feel it no longer needs to remember it?
options: Digital Amnesia (the Performance Paradox of Cognitive Offloading)
learnings.learning: The 'Performance Paradox' of Cognitive Offloading, also called Digital Amnesia, describes how the moment we write something down or save it digitally, our brains treat that as permission to forget it.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: In PCIe power management, which state is comparable to a computer screen turning off — less active, but able to quickly resume full operation?
learnings.learning: PCIe's L0s state is a very light sleep state, comparable to a computer screen turning off, designed for short durations of idleness while allowing the link to quickly wake up.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: What is the overall purpose behind having a spectrum of power management states, from fully active to deep sleep, in the PCIe standard?
options: To let a device efficiently manage power based on activity, saving energy while remaining responsive when needed
To enable automatic firmware updates during idle time
To increase the maximum data transfer speed of the device
To allow multiple devices to share the same physical connector
learnings.learning: PCIe's spectrum of power management states allows a device to efficiently manage power based on its activity level, saving energy while remaining responsive when needed.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe
